REJECT as written; ACCEPT after one explicit typing correctionThe new definition of  $E_{\rm pair}$  is broader than the pool used to prove its bound. Negative rotors also have original singleton endpoints, whereas
$$P_{\rm neg}
=
\{\text{phase01 U terminal endpoints}\}
\cup
\{\text{phase10 U upper outer corners}\}$$
contains only U endpoints.The accepted cap argument excluded rotor cap fillers. It does not exclude rotor singleton contacts with arbitrary original  $2P0T$  pairs.The minimal correction is:
$$\boxed{
E_{\rm pair}
=
\left|
\left\{
q\in P_{\rm neg}:
\operatorname{tile}(q)\text{ contains another original owner's exact }2P0T
\text{ profile}
\right\}
\right|.
}$$
With this definition, I accept the all-contact extension, including the preserved defect bound, the AA bound, arbitrary shared owners, and  $2c+2i\le E_{\rm pair}$ . There is no hidden reuse with  $H$ .If “original negative singleton endpoints” was intended as shorthand for this already-defined U-only pool, the required repair is a one-line clarification. Under its literal meaning covering all negative sources, the supplied proof has a missing geometric premise.1. The missing role is a negative rotor singletonThe standard rotor has a phase in which its central square is one original  $4P0T$  tile and its four outer tips are four original  $1P1T$  singleton occurrences. This is the negative rotor phase with four irregular endpoint slots in the supplied catalogue.Those endpoints are negative singletons, but they are absent from  $P_{\rm neg}$ . Consequently,
$$|P_{\rm neg}|=2K_{10}+2K_{01}$$
does not count all negative-source singleton endpoints.Moreover, the cap rotor barrier cannot simply be transferred to pair contacts.A concrete pair contact that has no original endpoint collisionNormalize a phase10 parent  $U(8,4,4)$ , with the stated physical row pairs
$$\{-1,0\},\{1,2\},\{3,4\},\ldots$$
and column pairs
$$\{0,1\},\{2,3\},\{4,5\},\ldots.$$
Translate the supplied rotor endpoint set by  $(1,2)$ . Its endpoints become
$$\begin{aligned}
\{&(2,4),(3,4),(3,5),(3,6),\\
  &(4,3),(4,4),(4,5),(5,5)\}.
\end{aligned}$$
Its central square
$$\{3,4\}\times\{4,5\}$$
is an aligned physical tile. Its four outer tips are therefore the negative rotor’s singleton occurrences.The rotor tip
$$q=(2,4)$$
lies in
$$Q=\{1,2\}\times\{4,5\},$$
which contains the parent’s exact original  $2P0T$  profile
$$\{(1,4),(1,5)\}.$$
Every rotor endpoint avoids the complete parent endpoint set: the parent’s bar is in rows  $0,1$ , and its stems are in columns  $1,8$ .Thus the broad pair-contact predicate admits a rotor singleton in endpoint-disjoint geometry. The near-stem obstruction used at a cap is absent at this interior bar pair.This placement is only an endpoint-disjoint partial configuration, not a complete feasible counterexample. Its retained supports require further owners; for example, the rotor support at  $(2,3)$  has both the rotor endpoint  $(2,4)$  and parent endpoint  $(1,3)$  as neighbors. I am not claiming that the displayed two-source union satisfies the complete feasibility hypotheses.Its significance is precise: the asserted inclusion of all pair-contact negative singletons in  $P_{\rm neg}$  does not follow from the supplied profile and endpoint-disjointness argument. To preserve the broad definition, one would need an additional theorem excluding every such rotor contact in complete feasible fusions, or a different injection accounting for them. Neither appears in the extension.2. With  $q\in P_{\rm neg}$ , the physical disjointness proof is completeLet  $\mathcal E$  denote the corrected set of pair-contact endpoints, so  $E_{\rm pair}=|\mathcal E|$ , and let  $\mathcal F_{\rm neg}$  be the set of negative cap filler points.The accepted cap classification and cap-tile uniqueness give
$$\mathcal F_{\rm neg}\subseteq P_{\rm neg},
\qquad
|\mathcal F_{\rm neg}|=F_{\rm neg}.$$
By its corrected definition,
$$\mathcal E\subseteq P_{\rm neg}.$$
It remains to prove that these two sets are disjoint.Suppose  $q$  belonged to both. Its unique fixed physical tile  $Q$  would contain:The cap owner’s exact original triple  $Q\setminus\{q\}$ .Another owner’s exact original  $2P0T$  profile, consisting of two points in  $Q\setminus\{q\}$ .Let  $C$  be the cap owner and  $B$  the pair owner.If  $B\ne C$ , their original endpoint sets overlap at the pair points, contrary to original endpoint disjointness.If  $B=C$ , the same original owner would have both exactly three and exactly two endpoints in the same physical tile. That is impossible.Therefore
$$\mathcal F_{\rm neg}\cap\mathcal E=\varnothing,$$
and hence
$$F_{\rm neg}+E_{\rm pair}
\le |P_{\rm neg}|
=2K_{10}+2K_{01}.$$
This argument is independent of dimensions beyond the established source catalogue. It allows arbitrary source counts, contact graphs, splits and recurring owners.Exact profiles and set counting are essentialThe phrase exact original  $2P0T$  profile is doing necessary work. If “pair” meant any chosen two endpoints inside a larger original profile, a cap triple itself would supply such a pair, destroying the exclusion.Set counting also resolves the internal multiplicity issue. A point is counted once regardless of how many descriptions refer to its contact. Two different foreign pair owners cannot both occupy its tile: their disjoint pairs would require four endpoints among the three corners other than  $q$ .Conversely, one original pair may witness two different singleton endpoints in the other two corners. Counting both endpoints is correct: the resource being counted is the original singleton endpoint, not the witnessing pair.A source may recur at different endpoints or in different roles. No owner-freshness premise is needed.3. The typed  $c/i$  occurrences are a distinct subsetThe earlier accepted geometric proof supplies exactly what is needed here.Each intermediate tip counted by  $c$ :Is an original phase01 U terminal endpoint, hence belongs to  $P_{\rm neg}$ .Shares its physical tile with its parent’s exact original  $2P0T$  profile.Each child corner counted by  $i$ :Is an original phase10 U upper outer corner, hence belongs to  $P_{\rm neg}$ .Shares its physical tile with that parent profile.The previously audited nonreuse argument establishes that all  $2c+2i$  designated points are distinct, including comparisons across different parents and between intermediate and child roles. Therefore they inject into  $\mathcal E$ , giving
$$2c+2i\le E_{\rm pair}.$$
No classification of the remaining elements of  $\mathcal E$  is required. This remains an all-contact count within the specified original U singleton pool.4. The preserved defect bound is valid, including nonfull tilesCombining the corrected pool inequality with the established cap identity,
$$F_{\rm neg}+F_{\rm pos}+U_0=2K_{11},$$
gives
$$2K_{11}+E_{\rm pair}
\le
2K_{10}+2K_{01}+F_{\rm pos}+U_0.$$
The absence of hidden reuse with  $H$  can be demonstrated by an exact identity, rather than only by interpreting the inequality.Define the unused singleton-slot count
$$L=
\left|
P_{\rm neg}\setminus
(\mathcal F_{\rm neg}\cup\mathcal E)
\right|
\ge0.$$
Because the two charged sets are disjoint,
$$2K_{10}+2K_{01}=F_{\rm neg}+E_{\rm pair}+L.$$
Substitute the cap identity to obtain
$$F_{\rm pos}+U_0
=
2(K_{11}-K_{10}-K_{01})+E_{\rm pair}+L.$$
Now insert this into the established reserve identity:
$$\begin{aligned}
2R
&=(F_{\rm pos}+U_0)+(A-F_{\rm pos})+Z_0+H\\
&=2(K_{11}-K_{10}-K_{01})
  +E_{\rm pair}
  +(A-F_{\rm pos})+Z_0+H+L.
\end{aligned}$$
Dropping  $L\ge0$  proves the proposed bound:
$$\boxed{
2R\ge
2(K_{11}-K_{10}-K_{01})
+E_{\rm pair}
+(A-F_{\rm pos})+Z_0+H.
}$$
The difference  $K_{11}-K_{10}-K_{01}$  must retain its signed integer meaning.Why a nonfull  $E_{\rm pair}$  tile does not spend  $H$  twiceA nonfull qualifying tile contains three endpoints: the original pair and a singleton of another owner. It is a mixed nonfull triple and contributes an  $L_3$  unit to  $H$ .Thus the same physical tile can indeed occur in the descriptions of  $E_{\rm pair}$  and  $H$ . That observation does not invalidate the displayed bound.The role of  $E_{\rm pair}$  is to exclude original singleton slots from use as cap fillers. The resulting global constraint is on  $F_{\rm pos}+U_0$ . The  $H$  term remains in the exact reserve identity throughout. The identity with  $L$  above proves that these contributions coexist without assuming geometric disjointness between  $E_{\rm pair}$  tiles and  $H$  tiles.What would be invalid is to treat  $E_{\rm pair}$  itself as a fresh defect reserve and add it independently to another lower bound for  $R$ . The extension expressly avoids that interpretation.5. The corrected AA bound holds over the same componentUse the accepted AA census and positive-cap exclusion over the same component as the counts in the conclusion:
$$F_{\rm pos}=0,\qquad U_0=0.$$
Then
$$F_{\rm neg}=2K_{11}.$$
The corrected pool inequality gives
$$2K_{11}+E_{\rm pair}\le2K_{10}+2K_{01}.$$
Therefore, with
$$\Delta=K_{10}+K_{01}-K_{11},$$

$$\boxed{E_{\rm pair}\le2\Delta.}$$
This also establishes  $\Delta\ge0$ . Consequently the natural-number subtraction in the conditional AA Lean statement is justified by its premises; it is not concealing an unrestricted signed deficit.Combining this bound with the distinct typed subset gives
$$2c+2i\le E_{\rm pair}\le2\Delta,$$
hence
$$c+i\le\Delta,\qquad 2i\le\Delta.$$
There is one additional, minor correction to the prose: §4 says the  $E_{\rm pair}$  conclusion follows by substituting into (1). Its upper bound requires the all-contact inequality (4). Equation (1) only provides the typed  $c/i$  bound; a lower bound  $E_{\rm pair}\ge2c+2i$  cannot upgrade that to an upper bound on  $E_{\rm pair}$ .6. If all negative-source singletons are intended, the bound must changeLet  $n_-$  denote the number of negative rotors, distinct from the event reserve  $R$ . The full negative-singleton pool has cardinality
$$2K_{10}+2K_{01}+4n_-.$$
The same cap-versus-exact-pair exclusion then proves the broader, weaker bound
$$2K_{11}+E_{\rm pair}
\le
2K_{10}+2K_{01}+4n_-+F_{\rm pos}+U_0,$$
and in AA,
$$E_{\rm pair}\le2\Delta+4n_-.$$
Removing this rotor allowance needs a new argument. Alternatively, split the broad count into U-owned and rotor-owned portions and apply the sharp stated formulas only to its U-owned portion.The three additional Lean declarations cannot resolve this typing issue: they assume the numerical pool inequality that the physical argument must establish. Their conditional arithmetic is consistent with the corrected proof. I make no claim about executing or independently validating the reported compilation, axiom audits or controls.Required repairs: explicitly define  $E_{\rm pair}$  using  $q\in P_{\rm neg}$ , and change the AA derivation’s reference from (1) to (4). With those repairs, the written extension is accepted for arbitrary legal complete source dimensions, counts and contact graphs, including shared original owners.The future strict-excess target must use that same corrected count. A proof of  $E_{\rm pair}>2\Delta$  for it would exclude the AA residual; such a proof has not been supplied. Full AA closure and unrestricted coefficient-one/grid conclusions remain open.
